text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prestigious international business publisher The Economist Group indicated yesterday it would be interested in an interest in the Fairfax business titles if the company were carved up under new media ownership rules. Representatives of the group have met with Government officials and potential partners in recent days. Page 1.

Another surge in United States stock prices, lower bond prices, and the expectation of increased corporate profits prompted a sharp rise in the Australian sharemarket yesterday, with the All Ordinaries index enjoying a jump of 20.1 points to close at 251.8 points, its highest ever level. Page 1.

Sales in upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd fell 3.2 per cent to A$290.5 million for the 13 weeks to April 26, and the company yesterday predicted difficult trading conditions would continue at least until the end of June. The poor result was blamed on continuing problems in apparel retailing. Page 19.

Sources close to the Colonial float say that after being forced to re-open the float, the group now faces the processing of nearly 80,000 applications for shares, with an extra 5,000 prospectuses being received after the Australian Securities Commission forced the re-opening. Page 19.

Queensland Cotton Holdings Ltd chairman Ben MacDonald said the company's peak net profit result of A$13.25 million to February 28, posted yesterday, shows a continuation of the company's trend of record results since its listing in 1992, and a positive peformance for the 1997/98 year is expected. Page 19.

The majority of stockbroking firms are advising clients with John Fairfax Holdings Ltd shares to sell now, as the recent surge in the company's share price has been pushed beyond reasonable levels, with a 2.9 per cent surge over the past week, and 7.3 percent increase over the past month, amid speculation Kerry Packer may soon bid for the company. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The international mining community is beginning to feel the backlash of the Busang gold fraud, with the Indonesian Government announcing it is proposing to take 10 per cent of every new resource project. Newcrest Mining Ltd managing director John Quinn sid the move will see a new outlook on the country from mining companies, with Highlands Pacific Ltd managing director Ian Holzberger saying the proposal would be of great concern. Page 23.

Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd Enterprises executive director Peter O'Connell said yesterday the group had received 50 separate proposals for gaming ventures following its withdrawal from the Sydney Harbour Casino involvement. O'Connell said the withdrawal did not quell PBL's enthusiasm to establish an international gaming division. Page 23.

Global investors have pushed stock prices higher in a day that saw the Australian All Ordinaries react strongly to another record-breaking performance on Wall Street. However, local analysts are reacting cautiously, with one saying the latest rise in the US seemed "a little starry eyed". Page 23.

Junior players involved in the exploration of the Gawler Craton in South Australia, who have already toughed it out after failing to deliver expected windfalls from initial drilling results, suffered in the washout from the Canadian Bre-X disaster, with Helix shares down six cents to A$1.38, Goldstream down one cent to 52 cents, and Minotaur also down one cent to 36 cents. Page 25.

Placer Pacific said yesterday it would not be deterred by the Busang gold fiasco, and would continue its aggressive Asia-based growth strategy. Spokesman Greg Germon said the situation had placed some doubt on what was going on, but the company believes the region is highly prospective. Page 25.

Despite the report this week that the Busang mine in Indonesia only reported traces of gold, Perth-based miner Golden Valley says it is not yet ready to walk away from the deposit. Chairman Warren Beckwith said a cautious step forward may be taken after data is looked at. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Opposition parties in the Senate have joined forces to protect the needs of low and middle income earners and are expected to water down the Federal Government's proposal to levy a 15 per cent superannuation surcharge, sending the A$1.5 billion expected from the levy into doubt. Page 33.

Former Labor Minister Graham Richardson has been hired by Rene Rivkin to promote his new newsletter the Rene Rivkin Report, with Richardson, who has been dabbling in the stockmarket since 1986 and more seriously in the last three years, saying Rivkin had done much to assist him. Page 33.

As the All Ordinaries rallied to 2513 yesterday in response to record highs in the United States, local investors were less enthusiastic than their American counterparts. Investors are trying not to read too much into the Dow Jones rise, as its only reflets price rises among the largest United States industrial stocks. Page 33.

The new managing director of David Jones, Peter Wilkinson, has blamed the decline in the demand in apparel and the decline in sales to three South Australian-based stores for the worst quarterly sales figures since November 1995. The department chain announced yesterday its sales fell 3.2 per cent to A$290.5 million in the 13 weeks to April 26. Page 35.

Fairfax newspapers deputy chairman Rodney Price said yesterday that his aim is to expand Fairfax not to break it up in response to rumours that the company's titles will be sold off separately. Speculation has been sparked by the suspected changes to cross-media ownership rules, but Price says Fairfax does not want to be the cause of media law changes. Page 35.

The general manager of motoring and insurance group NRMA, Lester Doecke, said yesterday he is confident NRMA can compete in the crowded home loan market after it was announced this week that the company will make its belated foray into the market this yea. However, industry participants argue that NRMA left it too late and lost a golden opportunity to enter the market while the non-bank lenders had a price advantage over the banks. Page 35.
THE AGE

Australia's All Ordinaries Index performed well on the back of a phenomenal bull run on Wall Street. The All Ords shot up to 2512.8, going above 2500 for the first time since March, and closing at a record figure. The good results were reflected across the board, with 17 of the top 20 stocks recording gains. Page B1.

Under pressure to strike a deal with shipbuilders to win Senate support for the abolition of production bounties for computer manufacturing, machine tools and books, Federal Industry Minister John Moore will meet with Australian shipbuilders in Hobart today in a move that is expected to see a further extension of the threatened ship building bounty. Page B1.

David Jones has issued disappointing figures for the last quarter, with sales falling by three per cent to A$290.5. The result has lead to the revision of plans for new stores in Fountain Gate and Auckland as directors warn of no prospects for improvementin 1997. Page B3.

The Victorian Power Exchange has issued statistics showing that if Victoria has summer weather this year similar to last year's, households could face up to 12 hours of blackouts. This could be remedied by the Newport generator becoming operational, and VX said the industry may offer financial compensation to the owners of the generator, Ecogen, in order to keep it open. Page B3.

Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge has given his approval for the Century Zinc project to get underway again prompting the managing director of the project, Ian Williams, to announce plans to make the first shipment of zinc concentrate by the latter half of 1999. The project will go ahead after Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander native title claimants negotiated an agreement with the Queensland Government. Page B3.

Queensland Cotton has released figures showing a 65 per cent rise in net earnings in its fifth year of record results. Shareholders have been rewarded with a financial dividend of 18 cents fully franked and chairman Ben McDonald said yesterday he expects profitability to continue. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
